clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: We have so many versatile defenders, athletes. We have so many good players that can do different things.

clips.speaker: Dean Wade
clips.text: We have so many great players, so many unstoppable people in transition. It is almost like a free throw or basket in transition. I think a big emphasis is getting out more in transition. The way our defense is, how many turnovers we can create, we should be unbelievable in transition. Especially with Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, all those guys, they get out in transition, those are hard people to stop. When you are out in transition, it makes everything a little bit easier. Your decision-making can be easier, you are going to see the open guy a little easier.
clips.news_angle: Dean Wade on the 76ers' transition offense potential
clips.social_post: The 76ers are prioritizing transition offense this year. Dean Wade says with players like Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the team should be unbelievable in the open floor.
clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: We have so many great players, so many unstoppable people in transition.

clips.speaker: Dean Wade
clips.text: They are unbelievable. They are so fast and quick. Tyrese Maxey, he gets out in transition and it is unbelievable how fast he moves, how fast he can change direction. I feel like the thing that really surprised me the most is they never make the wrong decision, they are always making the right decision. If that is dashing it out on the baseline, kicking out, scoring, whatever it is, they always make the right decision. That is hard, especially for a young guy. Tyrese Maxey is only in his second year, so seeing him, he is playing like he is a vet. He knows the right plays and he is doing it and he is not forcing anything.
clips.news_angle: Dean Wade on the decision-making of Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown
clips.social_post: Dean Wade is impressed by the maturity of Tyrese Maxey. He says Maxey plays like a veteran and rarely makes the wrong decision in transition, whether that means scoring or finding an open teammate.
clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: They never make the wrong decision, they are always making the right decision.

clips.speaker: Dean Wade
clips.text: I will not lie, it has not really changed our relationship. We still talk trash about our colleges and when we play each other and all the sports things. He is no different than what he was when I was in Cleveland. He is always checking in, seeing how my family is, I ask how his family is and he genuinely cares. So that is nice to see, but the change in title and everything has not changed him as a person. Seeing him as the top dog is always fun.
clips.news_angle: Dean Wade on his relationship with Mike Gansey

clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: He is no different than what he was when I was in Cleveland.

clips.speaker: Dean Wade
clips.text: There is a lot. The past few days, especially with Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the way they think the game is similar to the way I think the game, especially on the defensive end. When I get out on the same team as those guys, it is always something I kind of like to pick their brain. They have a thought, have a half-thought, very similar to the way I thought the game. When I see early, the past couple weeks, with Tyrese Maxey and those guys, I love the way he plays. I really do. Any time I get out there on his team, I love it because he is flying around in transition, he is making the right cuts, he is sacrificing shots.
clips.news_angle: Dean Wade on his defensive alignment with Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey
clips.social_post: Dean Wade says he loves playing alongside Tyrese Maxey because of his high defensive IQ and willingness to sacrifice shots. He notes that their defensive instincts are very similar.
clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: The way they think the game is similar to the way I think the game.

clips.speaker: Dean Wade
clips.text: I think a little bit of both. Kansas State when I was there, I think we were like a top-five defensive team in the nation and we played the same way we switched everything. I had to learn that pretty fast when I was at Kansas State. I was not really diving into my defensive ability then too much. I just did it good enough to get stops. In the NBA, it was a way to stick in the league. I was a two-way, I was undrafted. I had to figure out a way to kind of separate myself. I had great coaches when I was young in the NBA, a guy named Josh Broghammer and Chris Darnell were my coaches and they were counting on me. We sat down one time and they were like, if you want to stay in this league, every team has a scorer and a shooter, every team has somebody that can create. Not every team has a defender. You need to move good enough laterally, that is where you can stick if you want to stick in this league. So I took that conversation and I dove in headfirst into that.
clips.news_angle: Dean Wade on his defensive development and coaching influences
clips.social_post: Dean Wade reflects on his path to the NBA, noting that he had to commit to being a defender to stick in the league. He credits early coaching for teaching him that defensive versatility is the key to longevity.
clips.video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26
clips.pull_quote: Not every team has a defender. You need to like, move good enough laterally.
